parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one biomedical/genetic explanation of a phobia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one study about classical conditioning of a phobia, e.g. the study of little Albert.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the study you described in (b).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the treatment and management of depression.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate the treatment and management of depression, including a discussion of nature
versus nurture. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘persuasive techniques’ used in advertising.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the AIDA model of advertising.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one similarity and one difference between the AIDA model and one other model of
advertising.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about retail/leisure environment design.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about retail/leisure environment design,
including a discussion about demand characteristics. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘psychogenic pain’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the gate control theory of pain (Melzack, 1965).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two strengths of the gate control theory.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about measuring stress.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about measuring stress, including a discussion
about self-reports. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the ‘norming’ stage of group development by Tuckman (1965).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the theory of team roles in organisations proposed by Belbin (1981).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the validity of Belbin’s theory of team roles.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about motivators at work (intrinsic and extrinsic
motivation, types of rewards systems, non-monetary rewards).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about motivators at work (intrinsic and extrinsic
motivation, types of rewards systems, non-monetary rewards), including a discussion about
determinism.
